pages.html:
PART SIX

The Field Guide

Every leadership situation. The signal. What it means. Your move.

Building the Team

A TEAM MEMBER WHO USED TO RAISE CONCERNS HAS STOPPED

WATCH Their contributions in meetings have become shorter, safer, and less frequent over the past two months.

MEANS They have recalibrated the risk of genuine contribution. Something in the prior two months — a response to their input, a meeting dynamic, a decision made without engaging their perspective — taught them that genuine contribution is costlier than safe contribution.

YOUR MOVE Do not wait for the next meeting. Run a direct one-on-one: "I've noticed your contributions in meetings have changed. I want to understand if there's something about the room that's making it harder to bring your real thinking." The conversation this opens is the one that tells you what actually happened. Do not run this question in a group setting.

A NEW TEAM MEMBER IS PERFORMING ABOVE EXPECTATIONS EARLY

WATCH Their first three deliverables have been excellent and they are consistently ahead of schedule.

MEANS They are demonstrating capability and seeking calibration. The question they cannot ask directly: am I reading this environment correctly, and what should I be working toward that I cannot yet see?

YOUR MOVE Run Move 07 — bring them into the thinking that is one level above their current scope. "I want to show you something we're working through at the team level — not as a current responsibility, as context for how your work fits." This move builds Love and Profit simultaneously because it signals that you are investing in their understanding of the whole, not just their execution of their part.

TWO TEAM MEMBERS ARE IN OPEN CONFLICT

WATCH The tension between them is visible in meetings and is beginning to affect a third person who works closely with both.

MEANS The team's Tax account is building. Every meeting that runs with visible tension deposits Tax into everyone who witnesses it, not just the two people in conflict.

YOUR MOVE Address it directly with both parties separately before addressing it together. The individual conversations reveal what the joint conversation obscures. Run Move 06 — Pressure Reveal — with each person: "What's actually driving this for you?" The joint conversation, if needed, should happen after both people have disclosed the real source of the tension to you privately.

Developing Individuals

A DIRECT REPORT WHO RECEIVES FEEDBACK WELL IN THE MOMENT BUT DOES NOT CHANGE BEHAVIOR

WATCH They engage with feedback constructively in the conversation and the behavior recurs within two weeks.

MEANS Either the feedback is not landing at the level of behavior change — it is being received intellectually but not translated into action — or there is a structural constraint preventing the change that has not been identified.

YOUR MOVE Run Move 06 — Pressure Reveal: "When we talked about X, you understood the concern. The behavior hasn't changed. I'm wondering what's making it hard to change — not as a criticism, I want to understand the actual obstacle." This question surfaces either the translation gap or the structural constraint, both of which require a different response than another feedback conversation.

A HIGH PERFORMER HAS STOPPED ASKING FOR FEEDBACK

WATCH They used to seek input actively. In the last two months they have not asked for feedback once.

MEANS They have stopped expecting useful feedback from the asking. Either prior feedback has not been specific enough to be actionable, or something in the relationship has shifted their sense of whether honest feedback from you is safe.

YOUR MOVE Offer feedback they did not ask for, specifically: "I want to give you a piece of feedback that I think will matter for where you're trying to go." The unsolicited, specific, development-focused feedback from a leader is the move that signals you are paying attention at the level the high performer actually wants to be seen at. Do this before the pattern of not-asking has become the new norm.

A TEAM MEMBER IS PERFORMING WELL BUT ASKING FOR A PROMOTION THAT IS NOT YET WARRANTED

WATCH They are consistently meeting expectations and have expressed readiness for the next level.

MEANS They are measuring themselves against the current role rather than against the requirements of the role above it. The gap between where they are and where they need to be is not visible to them from their current vantage point.

YOUR MOVE Run Move 04 — Evidence Mirror. Do not say no. Say: "I want to show you what the next level actually requires and ask you to assess your own readiness honestly." Lay out the specific requirements. Ask them to evaluate themselves against each one. The person who can accurately self-assess the gap is the person who is ready to close it.

Navigating the Organization

AN EXECUTIVE HAS MADE A DECISION THAT YOU BELIEVE IS WRONG

WATCH The direction has been set and communicated. You have reservations you have not yet surfaced.

MEANS The reservation is being held privately, which means it is not available to be engaged with or to influence the execution.

YOUR MOVE Run Move 02 — Honest Strike — upward: "I want to share a reservation about the direction before we're too far into execution to address it." Name the specific concern, name the specific risk, and name what would change your read. Then give the executive the full picture and respect the decision that follows. The leader who surfaces concerns upward in specific, respectful, timely terms is the leader the executive actually wants in senior roles.

A PEER LEADER IS TAKING CREDIT FOR WORK THAT WAS COLLABORATIVE

WATCH In an executive presentation, a peer has described a joint effort as their team's work without acknowledging your team's contribution.

MEANS This is Tax being created in the peer relationship by a failure of attribution. Whether intentional or careless, it has a cost.

YOUR MOVE Address it directly with the peer, privately and promptly: "In the presentation, our contribution to that work wasn't mentioned. I want to understand if that was intentional and, if not, how we make sure it's accurate going forward." Do not address it in the executive meeting, in email, or to a third party. The direct conversation is the only move that resolves it without creating organizational politics.

THE TEAM IS PERFORMING WELL AND MORALE IS HIGH

WATCH Deliverables are strong, the energy in meetings is positive, and the one-on-ones are running with genuine exchange.

MEANS The score is high. This is not the time to coast — it is the time to invest at a level the team will remember when things are harder.

YOUR MOVE Run Move 03 — Intelligence Transfer — at the team level: bring them into something they cannot yet see. A strategic direction being considered. A market shift that will affect their work. A development opportunity that is not yet formalized. The team that receives substantive intelligence during a high-performing period builds the Love and Profit reserve that sustains trust through the difficult period that eventually follows every high-performing one.

Compliance ends when the authority does.

Trust does not.

The leader who has built genuine trust — in the one-on-one that went below the surface, in the performance conversation that was honest before it was unavoidable, in the team meeting where they said "I don't know" without flinching, in the executive conversation where they called before the problem became an escalation, in the exit conversation where they asked the question that most leaders never ask — that leader does not lose their team when the title changes or the organization restructures or the next opportunity arrives.

They lose some people. Good people leave. The high performer who is genuinely developed eventually outgrows the role and that is the correct outcome of genuine development. But the people who leave carry something with them: the standard of what a leader can be. And they become leaders who run the same conversations with their own teams. The leader who scores correctly does not just build a team. They build leaders.

The score that matters most in leadership is not the quarterly output metric or the engagement survey number or the retention rate, though all of those matter. The score that matters most is the one running in every conversation between the leader and the people they lead. Whether the Profit of genuine understanding is building. Whether the Love of specific, individualized investment is accumulating. Whether the Tax of the gap between stated values and lived behavior is being managed or is being allowed to compound.

That score is available to every leader, in every conversation, beginning with the next one.

Profit. Love. Tax.

Every room. Every person. Every conversation.

Craig Jones is the founder of the PLT Framework and the architect of the PLT Doctrine Series. He writes under the name Little Bunny. The PLT Framework was built from direct observation of how high-stakes conversations actually work — what gets exchanged, what gets built, and what quietly drains in the conversations that shape teams and careers. The Scorer: Leadership is the book in the series that reaches the widest professional audience and carries the deepest responsibility — because the leader who scores their conversations correctly does not just change their own outcomes. They change the outcomes of everyone they lead.
